subject.title: feat(memory-core): optional cross-encoder rerank stage for memory search

question: Should OpenClaw accept the new MemoryRerankProvider plugin SDK API, memoryRerankProviders manifest gate, exclusive single-slot behavior, and builtin-only rerank scope as a public plugin contract?
rationale: The implementation appears coherent, but the change creates a new third-party plugin contract and intentionally chooses product policy for exclusivity and qmd scope; automation should not decide that API direction.

options.title: Approve After Rebase Proof
options.body: Accept the proposed seam, require conflict resolution on current main, and verify the memory-core, plugin-contract, docs, and tsgo checks on the exact rebased head.

options.title: Revise The Public Contract
options.body: Ask for a smaller or differently shaped API before merge, such as a keyed provider registry, a newer capability-declaration mechanism, or explicit qmd parity requirements.

options.title: Pause Behind The RFC
options.body: Keep the PR open but blocked behind the RFC until maintainers are ready to sponsor the public SDK direction.

recommendation.title: Approve After Rebase Proof
recommendation.body: Accept the proposed seam, require conflict resolution on current main, and verify the memory-core, plugin-contract, docs, and tsgo checks on the exact rebased head.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision centers on public plugin SDK and manifest contract shape, and the history evidence ties steipete to those boundary surfaces.
